Getting Started

Six ways people get their first job in these fields

The routes that usually turn into full-time offers, and how long each one takes
Common starting routes

1. Summer Intern / Analyst (8–12 wks)

Common in software, finance, consulting, and corporate law. Strong performance here often leads straight to a pre-placement offer (PPO).

2. University Co-op (4–6 months)

Alternating semesters of classes with paid full-time work in automotive, aerospace, hardware, and biotech.

3. Articleship & Pupillage (2–3 yrs)

Required practical training under a licensed practitioner to qualify as a Chartered Accountant (ICAI / CPA / ACCA) or practicing lawyer.

4. Clinical Clerkship & Housemanship (1 yr)

Mandatory hospital rotations for medical, dental, and nursing graduates across wards, surgery, and clinics before independent practice.

5. Research Fellowships

Funded summer research programs (CERN Openlab, DAAD, Caltech SURF) where students publish early work before applying for a Ph.D.

6. Startup Apprenticeships

Short 3–6 month roles in small teams where you ship real work early alongside the founders.

Turning an internship into a job offer
  • Agree on what “done” means in week one: confirm the exact feature, report or experiment you will be judged on.
  • Write things down in public: clean pull requests, a short weekly summary, no surprises at review time.
  • Fix something nobody asked you to fix: broken tests, missing docs, a stale data pipeline.
  • Finish with a real demo: show the result, the numbers behind it, and what you would do next.
